gitarre.title: Guitar
gitarre.lead: P4: E2 A2 D3 G3 C4 F4. Tone, pulse and repeatable phrases of your own. Right hand uses only a pick; hammer-ons, pull-offs and tapping use the left hand.

keys.title: Keyboard
keys.lead: Melody with a steady accompaniment. Playable on synthesizer and piano.

p0.title: Foundation
p0.goal: Check clean note changes, P4 orientation, notation and pulse. Recall familiar skills briefly; practise specific difficulties.

p1.title: Tonic and phrase
p1.goal: Hear E as a reference. Shape small motifs through repetition, rests and variation.

k0.title: Foundation
k0.goal: Check touch, reading and basic coordination. One sound is enough.

k1.title: Tonic and phrase
k1.goal: A steady reference in the left hand, repeatable melody in the right. Deliberately distinguish Aeolian and Phrygian.

u0-1.title: Entry check: tone and pulse
u0-1.goal: Play four steady bars with clear note endings. Control fretting pressure and unwanted sounds.
u0-1.text:
Tune E2 A2 D3 G3 C4 F4. Listen with low gain first, then repeat with your usual sound. Distortion changes sustain and makes undamped strings more audible.

Position the guitar so your wrists can move freely. Fret close behind the fret with just enough pressure. Thumb position and picking movement may change with the task. Use both hands to mute unused strings.

Entry check: play four bars with a note on each of the first three beats and silence on beat 4. If stable, use these exercises as checks. Explore unfamiliar movements without a click first; then test them in time.

e0-1-1.title: Open strings: call and return
e0-1-1.instructions: Four bars A–B–A–C. E opens, A answers, E returns; D–E closes. Hold wholes for four quarters and halves for two. Mute the previous string at each change. Read names ahead, then play without aids.
checklist: String changes without overlap?
Whole and half notes held in full?
Return and ending without searching?
e0-1-1.position: Position I through fret 4, with open strings.

e0-1-2.title: Chromatic miniature: out and back
e0-1-2.instructions: A–B–A–C: two chromatic ascents, a return on the low string, then C–B–A to close. Frets 5–8 use fingers 1–4. Treat the semitones as passing notes and settle on the final A. Mute at string changes and release fretting pressure afterwards.
checklist: Notes equal in length and free of buzz?
Release fretting pressure between repetitions?
Unused strings silent?
e0-1-2.position: Position V, low E and A strings.

u0-2.title: P4: reference notes and intervals
u0-2.goal: Find E and C; hear and play minor thirds, fifths and octaves.
u0-2.text:
E A D G C F: adjacent strings are five semitones apart. A fifth needs seven: next higher string plus two frets gives 5 + 2 = 7. Minor third: 5 − 2 = 3. Major third: 5 − 1 = 4. Octave: two strings higher plus two frets gives 5 + 5 + 2 = 12.

These shifts work for fretted shapes wherever strings and frets are available. Open strings cannot move as open strings. Not every interval can be reached on the next string from every starting point.

Before each interval, imagine or hum the destination in a comfortable octave. Play it and compare.

e0-2-1.title: Find E
e0-2-1.instructions: Find E on the three lowest strings up to fret 12. Play and name the positions. Close the diagram and repeat in a different order. Then add the three highest strings. Then play the written A–B–A–C miniature. A returns exactly; C leads to the lower reference pitch. Locate each position first, then connect four bars in time.
checklist: E on the E, A and D strings recalled without searching?
Octaves recognised as the same note name at a different height?

e0-2-2.title: Find C
e0-2-2.instructions: Find C on the A, D and G strings up to fret 12. Play each C and the next E above it. Compare this major third with E–G in the following exercise. Then play the written A–B–A–C miniature. A returns exactly; C leads to the lower reference pitch. Locate each position first, then connect four bars in time.
checklist: Three C positions found without the diagram?
C–E and E–G sound different?

e0-2-3.title: Minor third and fifth
e0-2-3.instructions: Start with E on the A string, fret 7. Play G on the D string, fret 5, then B on the D string, fret 9. Play the minor third and fifth successively, then as two-note chords. Move both shapes down two frets: D–F and D–A. Sing each destination first. Then play the written A–B–A–C miniature. A returns exactly; C leads to the lower reference pitch. Locate each position first, then connect four bars in time.
checklist: E–G and E–B found without the diagram?
Shapes moved to D?
Target notes approximately sung before fretting?

u0-3.title: Reading I
u0-3.goal: Read short first-position phrases without stopping the pulse to search.
u0-3.text:
Guitar sounds an octave below its notation. The low open string sounds E2 but is written E3: in the space below the third ledger line below the treble staff.

Lines from bottom: E G B D F. Spaces: F A C E. B means German H; Bb means German B. Circled string numbers run from high to low: 1 = F, 6 = E. Finger 0 means an open string.

Read rhythm and starting pitch first, then the direction of neighbouring notes. Use aids for a first attempt, then hide them. Singing in a comfortable octave is enough.

Whole note: open head without a stem, four quarter-note beats. Half note: open head with a stem, two beats. Quarter note: filled head with a stem. Eighth note: one flag or beam, two per quarter. A dot adds half the original value. Rest symbols represent the same durations without sound. In 4/4, four quarter-note beats fit between barlines.

♯ raises a note by a semitone, ♭ lowers it; ♮ cancels the accidental. A key signature applies to the named notes in every octave. An individual accidental applies in its octave until the barline. Fretting fingers: 1 index, 2 middle, 3 ring, 4 little finger.

e0-3-1.title: Twelve bars on open strings
e0-3-1.instructions: Four three-bar phrases A–B–A–C: E–A–D, G–C–F, E–A–D, G–A–E. All six strings occur, with low E framing the piece. Read ahead and mute the preceding string at each change. Play once with aids and once without.
checklist: Read without note names or string numbers?
Changes on the first beat of the bar?
e0-3-1.position: Position I through fret 4, with open strings.

e0-3-2.title: C major: a small arch
e0-3-2.instructions: A–B–A–C in two-bar phrases: C–D–E–G, an upper-register answer, an exact return, and F–E–D–C to close. All notes are halves. Here the finger matches the fret; 0 means open. Read each phrase, then all eight bars without searching.
checklist: Recognised the return of A?
Kept the pulse after an error?
e0-3-2.position: Position I through fret 4, with open strings.

e0-3-3.title: New four-bar reading miniature
e0-3-3.instructions: Read four bars A–B–A–C: A presents the motif, B answers, A returns exactly and C closes on the tonic. Clap the rhythm first, then play without stopping. Correct the same version once before generating another.
checklist: Three new phrases read without searching pauses?
Repeated without aids on another practice day?
e0-3-3.position: Position I through fret 4, with open strings.

u0-4.title: Rhythm I
u0-4.goal: Hold note lengths and rests; re-enter accurately after silence.
u0-4.text:
Count quarters 1 2 3 4, eighths 1 and 2 and 3 and 4 and. Clap the written pattern before playing it on one note.

Count aloud on the first attempt, then count quietly and record the second. Rests remain part of the bar. In 3/4 the group starts again after three quarters; this does not automatically imply a waltz style.

e0-4-1.title: Quarters and halves
e0-4-1.instructions: Clap the rhythm, then play A–B–A–C. Repeat A exactly; B rises to A and C closes on E. Halves last two quarters. In the final bar, mute completely for the quarter rest on beat 2.
checklist: Note endings as accurate as attacks?
Two repetitions without losing a beat?
e0-4-1.position: Position I through fret 4, with open strings.

e0-4-2.title: Eighths and rests
e0-4-2.instructions: Four bars A–B–A–C on A. The eighth rest in B opens the phrase; after A returns, C closes with a half note. Clap and count eighths first, then play. Keep rests silent and hold the ending for its full value.
checklist: Even eighth notes?
Re-entry after the eighth rest on the correct subdivision?
e0-4-2.position: Position I through fret 4, with open strings.

e0-4-3.title: Triple time: a small minor melody
e0-4-3.instructions: Count 1 2 3. D–F–A forms A; G–F answers in B. A returns unchanged and C rests on D for three quarters. A dotted half is two plus one quarter. Sing before playing; do not add a fourth beat.
checklist: Return of the motif audible?
Final note held for exactly three quarters?
e0-4-3.position: Position I through fret 4, with open strings.

u0-5.title: Shape a sustained note
u0-5.goal: Distinguish straight tone from deliberately controlled vibrato.
u0-5.text:
Bending the string sideways raises its pitch; releasing the bend returns it to the original fretted pitch. This is not symmetrical movement below and above that pitch. Other vibrato techniques use different movements.

Start straight here and introduce small, slow vibrato later. This is an exercise constraint, not a universal rule: immediate vibrato can also work musically. Change width and speed separately, keeping hand and forearm mobile.

e0-5-1.title: Four bars, three tone variants
e0-5-1.instructions: G–A–G, then F#–E: a four-bar line on the D string. First play every note straight. Repeat with narrow vibrato from beat 3 of the whole notes, then with wider vibrato at the same speed. Keep F#–E calm. Compare the three recordings. Form: four bars A–B–A–C. Bar 3 returns to the opening motif; bar 4 provides the ending.
checklist: Vibrato returns to the original pitch each time?
Narrow and wide versions audibly different?
Other strings remain silent?
e0-5-1.position: D string: frets 5–7–5–4–2. Use the ring finger with position shifts for G, A and F#; index for E.

u0-6.title: Two voices: sustain and mute
u0-6.goal: Let an open bass string ring while the melody rests.
u0-6.text:
Two voices have independent durations. On the shared treble staff, melody stems point up and bass stems down. Whole notes have no stems. Read each voice separately, then combine them. Guitar still sounds an octave below the notation.

Use only a pick in the right hand. For a shared entry, place the bass on the pulse and pick the melody immediately afterwards: a deliberately brief spread attack. Mute unused strings when skipping or brushing across them. Never reattack a tied note. Then practise separate entries; tapping is not needed for these.

e0-6-1.title: Bass sustains, melody rests
e0-6-1.instructions: Four bars A–B–A–C over open E. Melody E, answer G, return E, ending F#–E. Each melody phrase rests through the second half of the bar while the bass continues. Briefly spread shared entries bass–melody with the pick. Stop both voices at the end.
checklist: Melody rest silent while the bass rings?
Both voices deliberately stopped at the end?
Two repetitions without unwanted string noise?
e0-6-1.position: Position II: melody on D string, bass on open E.

e0-6-2.title: Independent entries
e0-6-2.instructions: Bass on 1, melody from 2: E bass, A bass, return to E, ending F#–E over E. The melody always ends on beat 4. Mute the old bass at each change. The answer changes the bass; the ending changes the melody. Play four bars without extra attacks.
checklist: Bass and melody enter separately?
Previous bass muted at the change?
Melody ends on the correct beat?
e0-6-2.position: Second position: E3/F#3 on D; open E2 and A2.

u1-1.title: E as a reference, three notes as language
u1-1.goal: Hear a short idea, play it and repeat it exactly.
u1-1.text:
Begin each phrase on E and return to E. No looper is needed: the recurring tonic provides the reference. A drone of your own can be added later without changing the task.

Start with E, G and B. Hum, find them on the low E string and repeat. Then add the remaining E-Aeolian notes: E F# G A B C D. Steps to the octave: 2–1–2–2–1–2–2 semitones.

A scale run is orientation. Recognisable motifs, durations and rests turn this material into music.

e1-1-2.title: Three notes: idea and answer
e1-1-2.instructions: Invent four bars A–B–A–C from E, G and B on the low E string. A has at most three attacks, B answers with another ending, bar 3 repeats A exactly, and C ends on E. Leave space within the bars. Sing first, then play and record the whole miniature twice.
checklist: Sung contour matched on the guitar?
Motif recognisably identical twice?
Only the ending changed; rests retained?

e1-1-1.title: E Aeolian: call and answer
e1-1-1.instructions: A–B–A–C in two-bar phrases on the low E string. A circles E, B rises to B–C–D–B, A returns and C descends A–G–F#–E. All seven scale tones occur. Hold halves steadily and prepare position shifts before the next entry.
checklist: Semitone steps found without the diagram?
New note added without losing the motif?
e1-1-1.position: Low E string, frets 0–12; move the hand with the pitch.

u1-2.title: Three strings, one phrase
u1-2.goal: Play E Aeolian on E, A and D; move the same idea into a compact position.
u1-2.text:
This window uses open strings through fret 5 on E, A and D. Fretted notes: fret 2 with finger 1, fret 3 with 2, fret 4 with 3, fret 5 with 4. Open strings need no finger.

The score specifies the string. In particular, G3 stays on the D string at fret 5. Automatically choosing open G would leave this window.

e1-2-1.title: Three strings: motif and ending
e1-2-1.instructions: A–B–A–C on the three low strings. A rises E–F#–G–B; B continues to F#3. A returns exactly and G3–F#3–E3 closes. Prepare in second position, using open strings and finger 1 at fret 2. Let the final half note ring.
checklist: All notes on E, A and D strings?
Own motif recognisable in the new position?
e1-2-1.position: Open strings + position II through fret 5, E, A and D strings.

e1-2-2.title: Phrase, repeat, vary
e1-2-2.instructions: Four bars A–B–A–C in the three-string window: A is your familiar idea, B changes only the ending, A returns unchanged, and C ends on a longer E. Include at least one quarter rest in B. Play the form twice with half-time drums, then unaccompanied.
checklist: Planned target reached?
Rhythm changed while pitches stayed the same?
Secure entry after two bars of rest?

e1-2-3.title: New four-bar reading miniature
e1-2-3.instructions: Read four bars A–B–A–C: A presents the motif, B answers, A returns exactly and C closes on the tonic. Clap the rhythm first, then play without stopping. Correct the same version once before generating another.
checklist: New phrase without searching pauses?
G3 remains on the D string?
e1-2-3.position: Open strings + position II through fret 5, E, A and D strings.

u1-pedal.title: Pedal note and melody
u1-pedal.goal: Provide a bass reference and independent melody on one guitar.
u1-pedal.text:
A pedal note is sustained or reiterated while other notes move above it. Here E is the fixed bass. This is a small form of polyphony: bass and melody keep their own durations.

Play each voice alone first. Then repeat the bass once per bar with melody above. Do not reattack a tied note. Open E limits transposition here: moving the melody leaves the bass on E.

Low distortion and a quieter bass make the melody easier to distinguish. Then test the same passage with your usual sound. Chords, arpeggios and moving bass lines build on this later.

e1-pedal-1.title: Open E beneath a singing voice
e1-pedal-1.instructions: Melody is on the D string, with picked open E bass. At shared bar openings pick E2 first and the melody immediately afterwards. Melody E3 is tied into bar two: reattack only the bass. In the last bar end the melody two quarters before the bass.
checklist: Bass quieter than melody?
Held E3 continues through the new bass attack?
Final melody rest silent while the bass rings?
e1-pedal-1.position: Position II, D string: E3 with 1, F#3 with 3, G3 with 4. Open E bass.

e1-pedal-2.title: Your own answer over E
e1-pedal-2.instructions: Use the written example as a question and play it unchanged once. Keep the bass and melody rhythms, but change melody pitches using E3, F#3 and G3. End the answer on E3. Notate your version and read it on another practice day.
checklist: Bass unchanged; melody deliberately varied?
Answer repeated without searching?
Own notation matches what you played?
e1-pedal-2.position: Position II on D string, open E bass.

u1-3.title: Long notes and rests
u1-3.goal: Shape a phrase through duration, a focal point and silence.
u1-3.text:
A tie joins notes of the same pitch: attack only the first and sustain their combined duration. A rest ends the note. Ties and phrasing slurs are different signs; the notation distinguishes ties and legato slurs.

Emphasise a target through duration or attack. The highest pitch need not be the loudest. Compare two interpretations of the same motif.

e1-3-1.title: Ties
e1-3-1.instructions: A–B–A–C in two-bar phrases. A ties its second note across the barline; B opens the arch with B and C; A returns unchanged. C closes with a long E. Do not reattack tied notes; read each voice separately first.
checklist: No new attack under a tie?
Chosen focal point audible in the recording?
e1-3-1.position: Position I through fret 4, with open strings.

e1-3-2.title: Four bars of phrase, four of rest
e1-3-2.instructions: Use your familiar motif and lengthen one note as a focal point. Repeat the same phrase. Third attempt: a different focal point with the same pitches.
checklist: Motif recognisable despite longer notes?
Changed focal point changes the effect?
Secure entry after four bars of rest?

u1-4.title: Phrygian: F instead of F#
u1-4.goal: Hear and deliberately use the second scale degree as a colour.
u1-4.text:
E Aeolian uses F#, E Phrygian uses F; the other pitches are identical. This example retains a one-sharp key signature, so F receives a natural. An accidental applies to that pitch and octave until the barline.

F–E is our initial ending, not a universal requirement: F–G is a counterexample. The tension of F depends on bass, register, duration and accent among other things. No scale alone creates a band’s sound.

e1-4-1.title: F versus F#
e1-4-1.instructions: Four bars A–B–A–C: A uses F#, B replaces it with F, A returns, and C closes with Phrygian F–E. Keep rhythm and attack equal for the comparison. The key signature retains one sharp; the natural applies until the barline.
checklist: F and F# used in the correct version?
Difference audible without the diagram?
e1-4-1.position: Position I through fret 4, with open strings.

e1-4-2.title: Two paths through F
e1-4-2.instructions: Two bars of phrase, two of rest, using E, F, G and B. First end each phrase F–E. Then try F–G once and return to E later. Repeat the version that better matches your imagined sound.
checklist: Both endings deliberately tried?
Chosen version reproducible?
Pulse stays calm despite tension?

u1-5.title: Ear: from imagination to instrument
u1-5.goal: Find and notate a motif you have sung.
u1-5.text:
Record a short sung idea on your phone: three to five notes starting on E in a comfortable octave. Reproduce it without changing the recording in your mind while searching.

Clap its rhythm, find contour and pitches, then write them in staff notation. The recording remains the reference. Optionally use the same process on a short passage from your reference albums; a full transcription is unnecessary.

e1-5-1.title: Transcribe your own motif
e1-5-1.instructions: Sing a motif using E, G, A and B, record it and find it in the three-string window. Write rhythm and pitches on paper. On another practice day, read it and compare with the original recording.
checklist: Pitches match the sung recording?
Rhythm matches the recording?
Reproduced from your own score?

u1-6.title: Checkpoint: a small form
u1-6.goal: Develop and repeat a prepared musical idea.
u1-6.text:
Eight bars for one guitar alone: two motif, two answer, two variation, two ending. Open E bass on each bar’s first beat, melody on D and G strings. Second position up to fret 5: E3 F#3 G3 on D, A3 B3 on G. End the melody on E3.

Write two bars with both voices first. Read slowly, develop the form and record it. On another practice day, listen for independent note endings, steady bass and a recognisable melody. Then record without drums. If combining voices still stalls, return to the pedal-note unit.

e1-6-1.title: Eight bars of your own music
e1-6-1.instructions: Play the eight-bar miniature with your own bass voice. Bass once per bar; melody with long notes and a rest. Record with click or drums first, then alone. On another practice day, repeat from your notation.
checklist: Bass and melody remain independent?
Motif, answer and variation recognisable?
Rests and note endings controlled?
Repeated unaccompanied on another practice day?
e1-6-1.position: Position II on D and G strings through fret 5; open E bass.

ku0-1.title: Entry check: touch and pulse
ku0-1.goal: Play short phrases calmly and with control in each hand.
ku0-1.text:
Choose a sound with a clear attack. Sit with mobile forearms and wrists. Keep fingers loosely curved; arm and hand may support movement. Release keys at the end of their written duration, not automatically immediately.

Finger numbers apply to both hands: 1 = thumb, 5 = little finger. Play the two phrases separately. If secure without aids, move straight to coordination. Equal loudness is a control exercise, not an ideal for all music.

ke0-1-1.title: A-minor five-finger position, right hand
ke0-1-1.instructions: Four bars A–B–A–C in the five-note position A–B–C–D–E. A starts A–C–B; the answer rises to E. A returns and C leads C–B–A to the tonic. Keep fingers over their five keys, the wrist mobile, and sustain the ending for two quarters.
checklist: Pulse maintained without searching?
Notes roughly equal in loudness?
Hand stays mobile?

ke0-1-2.title: A-minor five-finger position, left hand
ke0-1-2.instructions: Four bars A–B–A–C in the five-note position A–B–C–D–E. A starts A–C–B; the answer rises to E. A returns and C leads C–B–A to the tonic. Keep fingers over their five keys, the wrist mobile, and sustain the ending for two quarters.
checklist: Bass clef read without names?
Written durations maintained?

ku0-2.title: One sound, one accompaniment
ku0-2.goal: Begin without having to program a sound.
ku0-2.text:
One polyphonic sound across the 49-key keyboard is enough. Choose a clearly articulated sound with short tails. Split, layer and arpeggiator are unnecessary for the initial work.

Listen for changes in volume or timbre when playing harder. Otherwise begin with rhythm, register and duration. A sustained synthesizer signal behaves differently from a decaying piano note.

Click and drums use the selected MIDI output on channel 10. An external sound source must receive drum notes there. The left hand plays its own bass.

ke0-2-1.title: Check sound and MIDI
ke0-2-1.instructions: Play a short note and a long note, then the same note gently and more firmly. Describe how the sound responds. Start the MIDI click and play four steady bars. Save the sound on the instrument if needed. Use the opening motif from the first written keyboard phrase (ke0-1-1): repeat the call twice, once more softly, then hold an ending note followed by a rest. Compare the sound response within this phrase.
checklist: Short notes and rests clearly separated?
Response to attack checked?
Click audible from the intended device?

ku0-3.title: Keys and intervals
ku0-3.goal: Hear and play five adjacent scale notes as a shape.
ku0-3.text:
A semitone is one adjacent key, including black keys. A whole tone is two semitones. E–F and B–C are adjacent white keys only one semitone apart.

Start with five-note spaces: A B C D E, then E F# G A B and D E F G A. Right-hand fingers stay 1–2–3–4–5. Full minor scales extend further; each exercise covers only the first five degrees.

ke0-3-1.title: A minor: five notes
ke0-3-1.instructions: Right hand: A4 B4 C5 D5 E5, fingers 1–2–3–4–5. Ascend and descend. Sing a three-note idea from these notes and reproduce it. Repeat the idea, then change only the final note.
checklist: Ascended and descended without searching?
Three-note idea repeated twice?

ke0-3-2.title: E minor: five notes
ke0-3-2.instructions: Right hand: E4 F#4 G4 A4 B4, fingers 1–2–3–4–5. Ascend and descend. Sing a three-note idea from these notes and reproduce it. Repeat the idea, then change only the final note.
checklist: Ascended and descended without searching?
Three-note idea repeated twice?

ke0-3-3.title: D minor: five notes
ke0-3-3.instructions: Right hand: D4 E4 F4 G4 A4, fingers 1–2–3–4–5. Ascend and descend. Sing a three-note idea from these notes and reproduce it. Repeat the idea, then change only the final note.
checklist: Ascended and descended without searching?
Three-note idea repeated twice?

ke0-3-4.title: Fifths and thirds
ke0-3-4.instructions: Left A2–E3 with 5–1, first successive then together. Right A4–C5 with 1–3, then replace C5 with C#5. Compare minor and major thirds directly. Make four bars: left A2–E3 as a half note on beat 1; right A4–C5 as quarters on beats 1 and 2, then rest on 3 and 4. Bar 2 uses C#5 instead of C5. Bar 3 returns to bar 1; bar 4 ends on A4 as a half note followed by two quarter rests. Hear call, colour change, return and ending.
checklist: Fifth reached comfortably?
A–C and A–C# deliberately distinguished?

ku0-4.title: Reading I
ku0-4.goal: Read both clefs within a small pitch range.
ku0-4.text:
C4 lies on the ledger line below the treble staff or above the bass staff. Pitches here follow MIDI: C4 = 60. Instrument displays may use different octave numbers.

Treble lines: E G B D F; spaces: F A C E. Bass lines: G B D F A; spaces: A C E G. B = German H, Bb = German B.

Hands separately first, then together. Clap new rhythms before playing. Read direction and intervals rather than decoding every pitch in isolation.

Whole note: open head without a stem, four quarter-note beats. Half note: open head with a stem, two beats. Quarter note: filled head with a stem. Eighth note: one flag or beam, two per quarter. A dot adds half the value. Rests last as long as the corresponding notes. In 4/4, four quarter-note beats fit between barlines.

♯ raises by a semitone, ♭ lowers; ♮ cancels the accidental. A key signature applies in every octave; an individual accidental applies in its octave until the barline.

ke0-4-1.title: Contrary motion from C
ke0-4-1.instructions: Four bars A–B–A–C. Both hands begin on C and move in opposite directions: right upwards, left downwards. A returns exactly in bar 3; bar 4 leads both hands back to C. Sing and play each voice alone before combining them.
checklist: Each hand secure without aids?
Note changes simultaneous?

ke0-4-2.title: New four-bar reading miniature
ke0-4-2.instructions: Read four bars A–B–A–C: A presents the motif, B answers, A returns exactly and C closes on the tonic. Clap the rhythm first, then play without stopping. Correct the same version once before generating another.
checklist: Three new phrases read in time?
Repeated without names on another day?

ke0-4-3.title: New four-bar reading miniature
ke0-4-3.instructions: Read four bars A–B–A–C: A presents the motif, B answers, A returns exactly and C closes on the tonic. Clap the rhythm first, then play without stopping. Correct the same version once before generating another.
checklist: Bass clef read without names?
Three new phrases without searching pauses?

ku0-5.title: Two hands, one pulse
ku0-5.goal: Sustain with the left hand; distinguish notes and rests with the right.
ku0-5.text:
Clap the right-hand rhythm first, then play the long left-hand notes alone. Combine one bar and extend only when each hand maintains its durations.

On piano the held bass decays; keep the key down for its written duration anyway. On synthesizer it may sustain. Both are appropriate for this task.

ke0-5-1.title: Whole notes against quarters
ke0-5-1.instructions: Left A2 as a whole note each bar, right A–B–A–C. In B, observe the right-hand quarter rest on beat 2 while holding the left. A returns unchanged in bar 3; C closes through C–B onto A. Use no sustain pedal: fingers determine each note ending.
checklist: Left hand sustains through the right-hand rest?
Both hands begin together on beat 1?

ke0-5-2.title: Eighths and rests
ke0-5-2.instructions: Four bars A–B–A–C on A. The eighth rest in B opens the phrase; after A returns, C closes with a half note. Clap and count eighths first, then play. Keep rests silent and hold the ending for its full value.
checklist: Rest audible?
Entry after the eighth rest in time?

ke0-5-3.title: Three-four, both hands
ke0-5-3.instructions: A–B–A–C in 3/4: A–C–E, an answer on C with a rest over E bass, return, then long A over A bass. Hold each left-hand dotted half for three quarters. Release fully during the right-hand rest. The next downbeat follows three beats.
checklist: Three quarters per bar maintained?
Bass changes align with the first beat?

ku0-6.title: Dynamics and note endings
ku0-6.goal: Shape a phrase through touch and articulation.
ku0-6.text:
On piano, attack affects the beginning of a note. Pressing harder after the attack cannot make that note louder. A crescendo requires successive attacks. Synth response depends on the program.

Sustain extends notes after keys are released. Start without pedal. The optional pedal task applies to piano or a sound that responds appropriately. Connected finger playing is the regular alternative without a pedal.

ke0-6-1.title: An audible dynamic arc
ke0-6-1.instructions: First play the four-bar melody A–B–A–C evenly. Then make A calm, B stronger, the return calm again, and C taper away. Change attack strength, not tempo. Compare both recordings; the ending on E lasts two quarters.
checklist: Dynamic arc or articulation contrast audible?
Stronger attacks do not change the pulse?

ke0-6-2.title: Connect notes, optionally with pedal
ke0-6-2.instructions: A–C–A–B–A in four bars: motif, answer, return, ending. Connect with fingers first. If a sustain pedal is available, change it after every new note: play the key, release the pedal and press again. Do not blur the preceding harmony.
checklist: Note changes controlled without pedal?
With pedal if available: old notes do not accumulate?

ku1-1.title: Tonic left, motif right
ku1-1.goal: Connect three notes into a repeatable melody.
ku1-1.text:
Start right hand E4, G4 and B4 with fingers 1, 3 and 5. Sing, play back and repeat a motif. Left hand initially E3 on each bar’s first beat; later E3–B3 together with 5–1. Hold without gripping.

Reattack every bar on piano and practise the same on synth. A separate pad is unnecessary. Add the full scale after the motif: right E4–E5 with 1–2–3–1–2–3–4–5. After G move the hand sideways and place the thumb on A rather than twisting it beneath a rigid hand.

ke1-1-2.title: Three notes over E
ke1-1-2.instructions: Sing and reproduce a three-note idea using E4, G4 and B4. Two bars melody, two bars left-hand reference only. Left E3 on every beat 1. Repeat the motif, then change only the ending. Four cycles.
checklist: Motif played identically twice?
Left hand steady during right-hand rests?
Change limited to the ending?

ke1-1-1.title: E Aeolian over a fifth
ke1-1-1.instructions: A–B–A–C in two-bar phrases. Right-hand A circles E, B rises into the upper register, A returns and C leads A–G–F#–E back. Reattack left E3–B3 calmly each bar. All seven Aeolian pitches occur; keep the melody audible above the bass.
checklist: Calm right-hand thumb change?
Left hand reattacks only on beat 1?
Motif extended by one note?

ku1-2.title: A melody breathes
ku1-2.goal: Long notes, clear rests and a shaped focal point.
ku1-2.text:
Ties join the same pitch: attack only at the start. The left-hand fifth is renewed each bar here, working equally on decaying piano and sustaining synth.

Shape a focal point through attack or duration; it need not be the highest pitch. Begin without pedal. Long reverb or release must not obscure the melody’s rests.

ke1-2-1.title: Ties over a steady bass
ke1-2-1.instructions: A–B–A–C in two-bar phrases. A ties its second note across the barline; B opens the arch with B and C; A returns unchanged. C closes with a long E. Do not reattack tied notes; read each voice separately first.
checklist: Right-hand ties correct?
Left hand steady and quieter than the right?
Chosen focal point audible?

ke1-2-2.title: Four bars of melody, four of bass
ke1-2-2.instructions: Develop the three-note motif with a longer target note. Repeat the phrase; on the third attempt change only its focal point. During the four-bar melody rest, keep the left reference going.
checklist: Motif recognisable?
Right hand silent in its rest while left remains steady?
Next entry on beat 1?

ku1-3.title: Motif and answer
ku1-3.goal: Make a connection audible with a small amount of material.
ku1-3.text:
Repetition gives the ear a reference. Then change exactly one property: ending, rhythm or register. A contrast becomes meaningful when something recognisable precedes it.

Double-note thirds come later. Keep one melody voice in the right hand here. On synth or piano, a clear melody over a steady bass can already be a complete musical thought.

ke1-3-1.title: One motif, two endings
ke1-3-1.instructions: Four bars A–B–A–C. A rises E–G–B; B answers and stays open on B. A returns unchanged and C closes G–F#–E. Keep left E3. Sing both endings, B and E, ahead and hear which continues and which arrives.
checklist: Repetitions rhythmically identical?
Only the last pitch changed?
Both versions recalled without the diagram?

ke1-3-2.title: Answer rather than run scales
ke1-3-2.instructions: Two bars of your motif using E4, G4, A4 and B4, then two bars of answer. One right-hand voice, left E3 every beat 1. Answer with the same pitches but a longer ending. Two identical cycles, then one variation.
checklist: Answer relates to the motif?
Bass steady and melody clear?
Repeated without searching?

ku1-4.title: Phrygian: F instead of F#
ku1-4.goal: Compare two colours over the same tonic.
ku1-4.text:
E Aeolian contains F#, E Phrygian F. In this example a natural cancels the key-signature F# in that octave until the barline.

F–E is one possible ending. F–G is a counterexample to the claim that F must always descend. Test both with the same rhythm and bass.

ke1-4-1.title: F versus F#
ke1-4-1.instructions: Four bars A–B–A–C: A uses F#, B replaces it with F, A returns, and C closes with Phrygian F–E. Keep rhythm and attack equal for the comparison. The key signature retains one sharp; the natural applies until the barline.
checklist: F and F# deliberately distinguished?
Left hand unchanged while right changes colour?

ke1-4-2.title: Phrygian with drums
ke1-4-2.instructions: Right E4, F4, G4 and B4; left E3 each bar. Two bars melody, two bass only. End F–E first, then try F–G and return to E later. Repeat your chosen version.
checklist: Both paths through F tried?
Chosen phrase reproducible?
Left hand in time?

ku1-5.title: From singing to playing
ku1-5.goal: Bring an imagined idea to the keys by ear.
ku1-5.text:
Sing a short idea from E, G, A and B in a comfortable octave and record it. Find the pitches on the keyboard afterwards. Keep the recording as the reference; do not unconsciously replace it with easier notes.

Write only the melody and rhythm in treble clef. Add left accompaniment after the melody matches. Optionally apply the same process to a short passage from your references later.

ke1-5-1.title: Transcribe your own motif
ke1-5-1.instructions: Record three to five sung notes. Clap the rhythm, find the melody with the right hand and notate it. Read it on another practice day and compare with the recording; then add left E3 each bar.
checklist: Pitches and rhythm match what you sang?
Recovered from your own score?
Melody unchanged when bass is added?

ku1-6.title: Checkpoint: a small form
ku1-6.goal: Play a repeatable miniature with melody and bass.
ku1-6.text:
Eight bars in E Aeolian: two motif, two answer, two variation, two ending. Left E3 or E3–B3 each bar. One right-hand melody with a deliberate rest; end on E.

Record with click or drums first. On another practice day, play unaccompanied and check a steady pulse: a bridge to any available piano. Use the same form on synth with suitable note endings. Check Phrygian separately with the same criteria later.

ke1-6-1.title: Eight bars for synth and piano
ke1-6-1.instructions: Play the eight-bar form twice. Right E Aeolian within E4–E5; left a steady reference. Listen on another practice day and change exactly one passage. Make the second recording without click or drums.
checklist: Motif and variation recognisable?
Melody clear above bass?
Rests audible?
Repeated without aids on two days, including once without accompaniment?

p2.title: Two-note shapes and arpeggios
p2.goal: Combine pedal bass, thirds and broken triads; read voices independently.

p3.title: Moving bass and lament
p3.goal: Move from a fixed pedal to a descending bass; keep the melody independent.

p4.title: Harmonic minor
p4.goal: Leading tone and dominant harmony; distinguish modal colour from tonal cadence.

p5.title: Sequence and figuration
p5.goal: Develop motifs through sequential repetition and broken chords.

p6.title: Contrasting colours
p6.goal: Use fourths and Lydian colour as deliberate contrasts.

p7.title: Rhythm II
p7.goal: Keep independent voices steady through subdivisions and changing groups.

p8.title: An arrangement of your own
p8.goal: Combine pedal notes, moving bass, melody, arpeggios and chords into a complete solo piece.

e0-4-4.title: Muted eighths, open accents
e0-4-4.position: Open low E; fretting hand helps mute other strings.
e0-4-4.instructions: Four bars of an E riff in A–B–A–C. Use alternate picking and light palm muting on short eighths; mute rests fully. On the second pass, play the first note of each bar openly. Let the final half note ring openly. Record both versions.
checklist: Pitch remains audible while muted?
Open accent only at the first beat?
Same pulse in both versions?

e2-1-1.title: Written study · Triads: minor and major
e2-1-1.instructions: Pick E bass first, then the upper three strings with a short controlled stroke. Keep unused strings muted. G3 and G#3 are on D frets 5 and 6; B3 and E4 remain fretted. Let the notes ring together after the spread attack. Form: four bars A–B–A–C. Bar 3 returns to the opening motif; bar 4 provides the ending.
checklist: Third change audible, other notes unchanged?
Two complete passes with clear releases?
e2-1-1.position: P4 · Frets 4–6; open strings as written. Show string cues when needed.

e2-1-2.title: Deliberate variation · Triads: minor and major
e2-1-2.instructions: Alternate minor and major without looking. Sing the new third before playing; keep bass and top-voice levels unchanged. Retain the written rhythm and form. Replace the minor third with the major third only in bar 2; bar 3 returns literally to the minor motif. Keep the ending of bar 4, so the comparison remains a piece.
checklist: New third sung before playing?
Unchanged elements retained during comparison?
e2-1-2.position: P4 · Frets 4–6; open strings as written. Show string cues when needed.

e2-1-3.title: Original application · Triads: minor and major
e2-1-3.instructions: Write eight bars with one triad per bar. Keep E bass and use one major bar as contrast. Place it deliberately within the phrase and play the same form twice.
checklist: Major contrast reproduced in the same place?
Notated, recorded and read again on another practice day?
e2-1-3.position: P4 · Frets 4–6; open strings as written. Show string cues when needed.

ke2-1-1.title: Written study · Triads: minor and major
ke2-1-1.instructions: Read rhythm and each voice separately first, then play the complete texture. Left E3; right G4–B4–E5 or G#4–B4–E5. Use right 1–2–5; only the thumb moves a semitone. Form: four bars A–B–A–C. Bar 3 returns to the opening motif; bar 4 provides the ending.
checklist: Third change audible, other notes unchanged?
Two complete passes with clear releases?

ke2-1-2.title: Deliberate variation · Triads: minor and major
ke2-1-2.instructions: Alternate minor and major without looking. Sing the new third before playing; keep bass and top-voice levels unchanged. Retain the written rhythm and form. Replace the minor third with the major third only in bar 2; bar 3 returns literally to the minor motif. Keep the ending of bar 4, so the comparison remains a piece.
checklist: New third sung before playing?
Unchanged elements retained during comparison?

ke2-1-3.title: Original application · Triads: minor and major
ke2-1-3.instructions: Write eight bars with one triad per bar. Keep E bass and use one major bar as contrast. Place it deliberately within the phrase and play the same form twice.
checklist: Major contrast reproduced in the same place?
Notated, recorded and read again on another practice day?

e2-2-1.title: Written study · Inversion and bass note
e2-2-1.instructions: Read rhythm and each voice separately first, then play the complete texture. Keep G3–B3–E4 above. Bass: open E2, G2 at E-string fret 3, B2 at A-string fret 2. Mute each previous bass at the change.
checklist: All three bass positions identified?
Two complete passes with clear releases?
e2-2-1.position: P4 · Frets 2–5; open strings as written. Show string cues when needed.

e2-2-2.title: Deliberate variation · Inversion and bass note
e2-2-2.instructions: Hold the top E across two bars while the other voices re-enter. Check that the bass still makes each inversion clear.
checklist: Long top voice independent of bass?
Unchanged elements retained during comparison?
e2-2-2.position: P4 · Frets 2–5; open strings as written. Show string cues when needed.

e2-2-3.title: Original application · Inversion and bass note
e2-2-3.instructions: Write eight bars using E–G–B–E bass twice. On the second pass change only the duration of the upper E. Play without drums and listen for a coherent form.
checklist: Bass path free of overlapping old notes?
Notated, recorded and read again on another practice day?
e2-2-3.position: P4 · Frets 2–5; open strings as written. Show string cues when needed.

ke2-2-1.title: Written study · Inversion and bass note
ke2-2-1.instructions: Read rhythm and each voice separately first, then play the complete texture. Retain the same right-hand chord; rehearse the written bass separately. Name the bass note and then the inversion at each change.
checklist: All three bass positions identified?
Two complete passes with clear releases?

ke2-2-2.title: Deliberate variation · Inversion and bass note
ke2-2-2.instructions: Hold the top E across two bars while the other voices re-enter. Check that the bass still makes each inversion clear.
checklist: Long top voice independent of bass?
Unchanged elements retained during comparison?

ke2-2-3.title: Original application · Inversion and bass note
ke2-2-3.instructions: Write eight bars using E–G–B–E bass twice. On the second pass change only the duration of the upper E. Play without drums and listen for a coherent form.
checklist: Bass path free of overlapping old notes?
Notated, recorded and read again on another practice day?

e2-3-1.title: Written study · Thirds with a melodic line
e2-3-1.instructions: Read rhythm and each voice separately first, then play the complete texture. For E3–G3 use A fret 7 and D fret 5. Then G3–B3 on D/G, A3–C4 on G/C. Move the hand with each change. Form: four bars A–B–A–C. Bar 3 returns to the opening motif; bar 4 provides the ending.
checklist: Major/minor thirds distinguished by ear?
Two complete passes with clear releases?
e2-3-1.position: P4 · Frets 2–7; open strings as written. Show string cues when needed.

e2-3-2.title: Deliberate variation · Thirds with a melodic line
e2-3-2.instructions: First balance both voices equally, then bring out the upper line with the same notes. Compare recordings at the same tempo.
checklist: Top line traceable in the recording?
Unchanged elements retained during comparison?
e2-3-2.position: P4 · Frets 2–7; open strings as written. Show string cues when needed.

e2-3-3.title: Original application · Thirds with a melodic line
e2-3-3.instructions: Invent a four-bar melody from G, B and C. Add a third below every second note only. Notate rests in the accompanying voice too.
checklist: Single notes and dyads alternate without hesitation?
Notated, recorded and read again on another practice day?
e2-3-3.position: P4 · Frets 2–7; open strings as written. Show string cues when needed.

ke2-3-1.title: Written study · Thirds with a melodic line
ke2-3-1.instructions: Read rhythm and each voice separately first, then play the complete texture. Right-hand thirds with 1–3 or 2–4; move the whole hand between positions. Quiet left E3 each bar. Also play the top line alone. Form: four bars A–B–A–C. Bar 3 returns to the opening motif; bar 4 provides the ending.
checklist: Major/minor thirds distinguished by ear?
Two complete passes with clear releases?

ke2-3-2.title: Deliberate variation · Thirds with a melodic line
ke2-3-2.instructions: First balance both voices equally, then bring out the upper line with the same notes. Compare recordings at the same tempo.
checklist: Top line traceable in the recording?
Unchanged elements retained during comparison?

ke2-3-3.title: Original application · Thirds with a melodic line
ke2-3-3.instructions: Invent a four-bar melody from G, B and C. Add a third below every second note only. Notate rests in the accompanying voice too.
checklist: Single notes and dyads alternate without hesitation?
Notated, recorded and read again on another practice day?

e2-4-1.title: Written study · Arpeggio above a bass
e2-4-1.instructions: The pick plays both bass and upper figure. At a shared entry, place bass on the pulse and the upper note immediately after it. Continue the written eighths with small string crossings while the bass rings. Bring out the top note without reattacking the bass. Form: four bars A–B–A–C. Bar 3 returns to the opening motif; bar 4 provides the ending.
checklist: Eighths even through chord changes?
Two complete passes with clear releases?
e2-4-1.position: P4 · Frets 2–5; open strings as written. Show string cues when needed.

e2-4-2.title: Deliberate variation · Arpeggio above a bass
e2-4-2.instructions: Play the same pattern accenting first its opening note, then its highest note. Keep bass quiet and eighths even.
checklist: Accent change without an extra bass attack?
Unchanged elements retained during comparison?
e2-4-2.position: P4 · Frets 2–5; open strings as written. Show string cues when needed.

e2-4-3.title: Original application · Arpeggio above a bass
e2-4-3.instructions: Write Em–C–G–Em twice as an eight-bar form. Use quarters first, then eighths, with the same chords. Finish together with the bass.
checklist: Denser second half at the same basic pulse?
Notated, recorded and read again on another practice day?
e2-4-3.position: P4 · Frets 2–5; open strings as written. Show string cues when needed.

ke2-4-1.title: Written study · Arpeggio above a bass
ke2-4-1.instructions: Read rhythm and each voice separately first, then play the complete texture. Prepare the right-hand triad, starting with 1–3–5–3. Left hand only at bar starts. Loop one bar before adding chord changes. Form: four bars A–B–A–C. Bar 3 returns to the opening motif; bar 4 provides the ending.
checklist: Eighths even through chord changes?
Two complete passes with clear releases?

ke2-4-2.title: Deliberate variation · Arpeggio above a bass
ke2-4-2.instructions: Play the same pattern accenting first its opening note, then its highest note. Keep bass quiet and eighths even.
checklist: Accent change without an extra bass attack?
Unchanged elements retained during comparison?

ke2-4-3.title: Original application · Arpeggio above a bass
ke2-4-3.instructions: Write Em–C–G–Em twice as an eight-bar form. Use quarters first, then eighths, with the same chords. Finish together with the bass.
checklist: Denser second half at the same basic pulse?
Notated, recorded and read again on another practice day?

e2-6-1.title: Written study · Power chords and muting
e2-6-1.instructions: Read rhythm and each voice separately first, then play the complete texture. E5: open E/A fret 2; A5: open A/D fret 2; B5: A fret 2/D fret 4. Strike only those strings. Use both hands to stop rests.
checklist: Only the intended two strings audible?
Two complete passes with clear releases?
e2-6-1.position: P4 · Frets 2–4; open strings as written. Show string cues when needed.

e2-6-2.title: Deliberate variation · Power chords and muting
e2-6-2.instructions: Repeat with palm muting, opening only beat 1 of each bar. Use low gain first, then your normal tone. Match comparison levels.
checklist: Open/muted changes tone rather than pulse?
Unchanged elements retained during comparison?
e2-6-2.position: P4 · Frets 2–4; open strings as written. Show string cues when needed.

e2-6-3.title: Original application · Power chords and muting
e2-6-3.instructions: Build eight bars from E5 and A5. Place one quarter rest in each bar, varying its position. Notate attacks and rests, then repeat from memory.Introduce a short motif and its answer in the first two bars. The last two bring a return and a deliberate ending; in an eight-bar piece each part spans two bars.
checklist: All written rests genuinely silent?
Notated, recorded and read again on another practice day?
e2-6-3.position: P4 · Frets 2–4; open strings as written. Show string cues when needed.

e2-rhythm-1.title: Written study · Short chords and offbeats
e2-rhythm-1.instructions: Use a short pick stroke across the upper three strings on the offbeat. Release fretting pressure at note-off and control open bass strings. Pick the bass separately on its written beat. Do not fill the eighth rest before the chord with an attack. Form: four bars A–B–A–C. Bar 3 returns to the opening motif; bar 4 provides the ending.
checklist: Chords precisely between clicks?
Two complete passes with clear releases?
e2-rhythm-1.position: P4 · Frets 2–5; open strings as written. Show string cues when needed.

e2-rhythm-2.title: Deliberate variation · Short chords and offbeats
e2-rhythm-2.instructions: Accent only the offbeat after beat 2. Clap first, then play the same chords. Keep bass and the other offbeats at their original levels.
checklist: Only the selected offbeat accented?
Unchanged elements retained during comparison?
e2-rhythm-2.position: P4 · Frets 2–5; open strings as written. Show string cues when needed.

e2-rhythm-3.title: Original application · Short chords and offbeats
e2-rhythm-3.instructions: Invent four bars with two offbeat chords and two omitted offbeats in each. Notate the rests and repeat the pattern over Em and C.
checklist: Omissions repeatable and bass stable?
Notated, recorded and read again on another practice day?
e2-rhythm-3.position: P4 · Frets 2–5; open strings as written. Show string cues when needed.

ke2-rhythm-1.title: Written study · Short chords and offbeats
ke2-rhythm-1.instructions: Read rhythm and each voice separately first, then play the complete texture. Right-hand chords are short while the left holds. No sustain pedal. Release with small movements rather than lifting the whole hand high. Form: four bars A–B–A–C. Bar 3 returns to the opening motif; bar 4 provides the ending.
checklist: Chords precisely between clicks?
Two complete passes with clear releases?

ke2-rhythm-2.title: Deliberate variation · Short chords and offbeats
ke2-rhythm-2.instructions: Accent only the offbeat after beat 2. Clap first, then play the same chords. Keep bass and the other offbeats at their original levels.
checklist: Only the selected offbeat accented?
Unchanged elements retained during comparison?

ke2-rhythm-3.title: Original application · Short chords and offbeats
ke2-rhythm-3.instructions: Invent four bars with two offbeat chords and two omitted offbeats in each. Notate the rests and repeat the pattern over Em and C.
checklist: Omissions repeatable and bass stable?
Notated, recorded and read again on another practice day?

e2-5-1.title: Written study · Hear a triad, build a phrase
e2-5-1.instructions: Read rhythm and each voice separately first, then play the complete texture. Play the upper line first on D/G/C strings. Add bass only at written bar starts. E can remain an audible reference through Em–C. Form: four bars A–B–A–C. Bar 3 returns to the opening motif; bar 4 provides the ending.
checklist: Chord changes audible in the melody?
Two complete passes with clear releases?
e2-5-1.position: P4 · Frets 2–5; open strings as written. Show string cues when needed.

e2-5-2.title: Deliberate variation · Hear a triad, build a phrase
e2-5-2.instructions: Listen to the preview once. Hide the score and write the four closing notes from memory. Compare with the example afterwards.
checklist: Closing notes written before checking?
Unchanged elements retained during comparison?
e2-5-2.position: P4 · Frets 2–5; open strings as written. Show string cues when needed.

e2-5-3.title: Original application · Hear a triad, build a phrase
e2-5-3.instructions: Compose eight bars: two motif, two answer, two arpeggio, two ending. Use Em and C, at least one melodic rest and one held bass note. Notate both voices.
checklist: Original form played twice without searching?
Notated, recorded and read again on another practice day?
e2-5-3.position: P4 · Frets 2–5; open strings as written. Show string cues when needed.

ke2-5-1.title: Written study · Hear a triad, build a phrase
ke2-5-1.instructions: Read rhythm and each voice separately first, then play the complete texture. Sing and play the right-hand melody alone first. Name left-hand bass notes before combining. Write down your fingering and keep it consistent. Form: four bars A–B–A–C. Bar 3 returns to the opening motif; bar 4 provides the ending.
checklist: Chord changes audible in the melody?
Two complete passes with clear releases?

ke2-5-2.title: Deliberate variation · Hear a triad, build a phrase
ke2-5-2.instructions: Listen to the preview once. Hide the score and write the four closing notes from memory. Compare with the example afterwards.
checklist: Closing notes written before checking?
Unchanged elements retained during comparison?

ke2-5-3.title: Original application · Hear a triad, build a phrase
ke2-5-3.instructions: Compose eight bars: two motif, two answer, two arpeggio, two ending. Use Em and C, at least one melodic rest and one held bass note. Notate both voices.
checklist: Original form played twice without searching?
Notated, recorded and read again on another practice day?

e3-1-1.title: Written study · Lamento: a descending bass
e3-1-1.instructions: Eight bars: the lament bass E–D–C–B twice. The second melody phrase starts with longer notes; in the last bar bass and melody return to E after two quarters. Sing the bass, then the melody, and finally combine both voices.
checklist: Bass line without clipped endings?
Two complete passes with clear releases?
e3-1-1.position: P4 · Frets 1–7; open strings as written. Show string cues when needed.
